sources.field_scope: Fishing-guide concession explainer. One guide card and one hang tag per application. Navajo Lake $500 with one vehicle hang tag. Other parks $300 with one vehicle hang tag. Fee line repeats $300 except Navajo Lake at $500. Permit year April 1 through March 31. Fishing license, tax identification number, and Secretary of State good standing required. Insurance minimum $1,000,000 each occurrence and $2,000,000 general aggregate, naming the State, the department, the division, and the property owner. Boating knowledge is preferred. Only one guide on the water at a time. Additional-card fee is mentioned and not priced. Business may not start until guide cards are in hand. Trip-ticket login goes to the permit holder.
sources.attribution: Department disclaimer. No separate license on this page.
sources.request_process: Download the application and submit it to the park manager. Headquarters issues the permit, vehicle tag, and guide card after approval. No public-records request was submitted.

sources.field_scope: Replacement text of 18.17.2 NMAC. Section 18.17.2.16 G prohibits motorized vessels on the San Juan River inside Navajo Lake State Park and authorizes non-motorized vessels from the Texas Hole day-use area downstream for fishing unless the director authorizes otherwise. A February 2024 packet with a blank effective date was not used as the in-force text.

sources.field_scope: Older fishing overview. Says the first 4 miles below Navajo Dam are special trout water, the first 3.5 miles are catch-and-release, and 17 miles are managed for rainbow and brown trout. Not merged with the 2026-2027 booklet. Not a roster.

Park page. Names Pine and Sims as the two marinas and points fishing guides to the public lookup. Those marinas are lake facilities. The page is not a business roster and not the river-rule departure.
Park map. Names Texas Hole, Crusher Hole, Cottonwood, Munoz/Lower Flats, Simon Point, a Bureau of Reclamation day-use area, Pumphouse, Pine, and Sims. Place names only. Not a business roster.

Navajo Lake alerts. Boating conditions Good. Elevation 6,072 feet, surface 14,006 acres, volume 1,508,500 acre-feet, last updated 2026-11-09. Highway 539 mile markers 0-5 closed. Crusher Hole day-use construction marked ongoing since 2025-01-22. The park telephone was not copied. Not a guide roster.

Crusher Hole day-use construction notice. Work began January 2025 and was described as continuing through summer 2026. The work area is fenced. The notice says the boat ramp and existing parking remain open. The alerts page still marks the item ongoing. The contact line was not copied.

Lake-conditions narrative with a latest-update line of 11/9/26. Navajo paragraph: elevation from 6,021 to 6,044 feet, storage 1,110,990 acre-feet, Pine open, Sims being adjusted, both ramps accessible with damage, release 250 cubic feet per second, river murky. Campground dates in this paragraph differ from the announcements index. Figures conflict with the alerts page and were not merged.

Announcements index. Navajo seasonal campground closure posted 2026-11-18 through 2027-01-31 for Cottonwood, Crusher Hole, Juniper, Cedar, and Sims upper loop. Pine main and Sims main loops remain by reservation. Not merged with the lake-conditions paragraph. Not a statement that day-use fishing is closed. Telephone numbers were not copied.
Release dated 2026-11-19. Says Navajo Lake rose sharply and points to the lake-conditions page. Not a guide roster. Does not reconcile the two November 9 elevation figures.

Fishing-rules booklet labeled 2026-2027. Special trout water from Navajo Dam downstream 3.75 miles to Crusher Hole day use, with a two-fly limit. Specific-waters line: no bag or possession limit for channel catfish or striped bass below the dam, and only two flies per line in special trout water. Extracts do not assign a chile color or a catch-and-release bag. Motorized vessels of any length must be registered through the Motor Vehicle Division. Motorized and sail-powered vessels 10 feet or longer need a title. Not a guide roster.
